stem:
A student investigates the sound from a horn attached to a car, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

A microphone is placed at the side of the road and connected to a frequency meter. The car travels towards the microphone. The frequency *f* of the sound detected by the microphone is read from the frequency meter.

The speed of the car is measured by two speed detectors. The two measurements of speed are *v*₁ and *v*₂. The average speed *v* of the car is determined from *v*₁ and *v*₂.

The experiment is repeated for different speeds of the car.

It is suggested that *f* and *v* are related by the equation

$f = \frac{f_s k}{k-v}$

where *f*ₛ is the frequency of the sound emitted by the horn and *k* is a constant.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of $\frac{1}{f}$ on the y-axis against *v* on the x-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and y-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *v*₁, *v*₂ and *f* are given in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f2]]

Calculate and record values of *v* / m s⁻¹ and $\frac{1}{f}$ / 10⁻³ Hz⁻¹ in Table 2.1. Include the absolute uncertainties in *v*.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of $\frac{1}{f}$ / 10⁻³ Hz⁻¹ against *v* / m s⁻¹. Include error bars for *v*.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the *y*-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of *f*ₛ and *k*. Include appropriate units.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: The experiment is repeated. Determine the speed *v* that gives a value of *f* of 987.8 Hz.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1 (not to scale)
figures.alt: A car with a horn travels towards a roadside microphone connected by cable to a frequency meter displaying 894.2 Hz.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A table gives values of v₁, v₂ and f, with blank columns for v and 1/f.
A blank graph grid has a vertical axis labelled 1/f / 10⁻³ Hz⁻¹ and a horizontal axis labelled v / m s⁻¹.
